investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining allocatable VM slots, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-bearing nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract defined in check-expectations.json line 256 to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion: the 2 nodes that carry this resource have no remaining allocatable VM slots, likely because existing remote agent pods are consuming all available peer-pod VM capacity and have not been released.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector, which could indicate a label was removed, a node pool was scaled down, or the pod spec's affinity rules were tightened in a recent deployment.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of nodes carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 of 6) may be insufficient for the current load or for concurrent eval runs, and no auto-scaling event resolved the shortage within the eval timeout window.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie remote agent pods from prior eval runs holding VM slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) failed in a previous run, orphaned pods may be occupying the remaining VM capacity.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval immediately succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), the failure was transient and not a sustained resource exhaustion.

If kubectl inspection shows the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes have free allocatable VM slots, resource exhaustion is not the cause and the scheduling failure may be due to a pod spec change (affinity, toleration, or resource request mismatch).
If all 6 nodes satisfy the pod's node affinity and selector, the 4-node exclusion is not a label/selector issue but rather a broader cluster misconfiguration.
If no orphaned remote agent pods are found consuming VM slots, leaked cleanup is not a contributing factor.

If the failure message changes on re-run (e.g., a different error or a timeout without the Unschedulable reason), the root cause may be a transient API or network issue rather than a scheduling constraint.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity across all nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct signal rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add an eval that counts running pods requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm and alerts when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold, providing early warning before full exhaustion.
Add a node-affinity conformance eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote agent pod's selector and affinity rules, catching label drift before it blocks scheduling.
Add a cleanup-verification eval that checks for orphaned remote agent pods (pods in Pending or Running state older than a configurable TTL) and fails if any are found, catching leaked eval resources.
Add a historical baseline to the remote-agent-create check (populate previousStatuses) so that currentlyRegressedFromPass can be computed and regressions are distinguished from persistent failures.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-05T21:22–21:27Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting zero available nodes: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod request is immediately rejected as Unschedulable. This prevents agent creation from completing, which in turn prevents the state-polling eval from ever reaching the point where it can collect and return orgId, agentId, readyState, and state evidence. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

investigation.title: Remote Agent VM Pool Exhausted: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the requested pod due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. The eval probe never reached the point of creating an agent or receiving a runtime response, so all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the resulting pod was left Unschedulable for 135–147 seconds across all three checks before timing out. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, no agent was created, and no runtime response was returned, causing a complete contract gap for all required evidence fields. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent VM node pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining allocatable VM slots, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-bearing nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract defined in check-expectations.json line 256 to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion: the 2 nodes that carry this resource have no remaining allocatable VM slots, likely because existing remote agent pods are consuming all available peer-pod VM capacity and have not been released.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector, which could indicate a label was removed, a node pool was scaled down, or the pod spec's affinity rules were tightened in a recent deployment.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of nodes carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 of 6) may be insufficient for the current load or for concurrent eval runs, and no auto-scaling event resolved the shortage within the eval timeout window.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie remote agent pods from prior eval runs holding VM slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) failed in a previous run, orphaned pods may be occupying the remaining VM capacity.

investigations.title: Remote Agent VM Pool Exhausted: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the requested pod due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. The eval probe never reached the point of creating an agent or receiving a runtime response, so all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the resulting pod was left Unschedulable for 135–147 seconds across all three checks before timing out. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, no agent was created, and no runtime response was returned, causing a complete contract gap for all required evidence fields. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent VM node pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior eval run left VM slots occupied, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. All three checks report identical 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' messages, strongly supporting this as the immediate cause.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are at capacity, no fallback exists and preemption is blocked.

TERTIARY — VM slots leaked by a previous eval run or other workload: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs) did not fully release VM resources from a prior run, the pool may have been partially exhausted before this run began.

SPECULATIVE — Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote-agent eval load: with only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, simultaneous execution of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime probes may exceed available VM slots even under normal conditions.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the 2 affinity-matching nodes immediately to determine whether the pool is currently exhausted or has recovered.
Audit all pods currently consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources to identify any leaked or stuck pods from prior eval runs that withCleanup may not have released.
If VM slots are confirmed exhausted, either scale up the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on existing nodes or add additional nodes with the required affinity labels to increase the schedulable pool.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration on remote-agent pods to determine whether the 4-node exclusion is intentional or whether additional nodes could be made eligible to increase scheduling headroom.

Investigate whether concurrent execution of all three remote-agent probes (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) in the same eval run exceeds the available VM slot count, and consider serializing or staggering these checks if pool capacity is limited.
Verify that the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs reliably releases VM resources even when a probe times out or fails mid-execution, to prevent slot leakage across runs.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is sustained or was a transient capacity spike. A pass on re-run suggests transient exhaustion; a repeat fail confirms sustained pool saturation.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly proves or disproves the VM slot exhaustion hypothesis by showing current capacity on the 2 affinity-matching nodes.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether leaked or long-running pods from prior eval runs are consuming VM slots that should have been released by withCleanup.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check for pending pods from this or prior eval runs
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Reveals whether unscheduled pods from this run or previous runs are still queued and holding resource reservations.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agent sibling checks together to confirm shared dependency failure
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If all three fail again with the same Unschedulable message, it confirms the shared VM pool is the common dependency. If only one fails, it narrows the cause to a check-specific issue.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed ample free kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the affinity-matching nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or admission cause would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check had passed while remote-agent-runtime failed, a shared VM pool exhaustion cause would be less likely and a check-specific configuration issue would be more likely.
If a re-run of the probe immediately after this failure succeeded without any infrastructure changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained pool exhaustion.
If the pod spec's node affinity/selector matched more than 2 nodes, the 4-node exclusion would not be a contributing factor to the capacity ceiling.

If evidence fields (orgId, agentId) were partially present in the failed check output, it would indicate the agent was created but the runtime call failed, pointing away from a scheduling cause and toward a runtime or network issue.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all remote-agent-eligible nodes before attempting agent creation, and fails fast with a capacity-specific message if headroom is below a threshold.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no kata.peerpods.io/vm-consuming pods remain after the remote-agent probe suite completes, catching withCleanup failures before they affect subsequent runs.

Add a node-pool health check eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote-agent pod affinity/selector meets a minimum threshold, alerting if the eligible node count drops below the expected value.
Consider a dedicated eval that measures VM slot utilization over time to detect gradual pool exhaustion trends before they cause full scheduling failures.
